answer: Mutual-bond sponsorship: a new agent enters the economy only when an established agent co-signs it, locking its own stake as collateral - a jade seal of trust that costs real money. If the newcomer fakes work or spawns fake identities, both bonds are slashed, so sponsors vet carefully instead of rubber-stamping. A Sybil attacker must cross a canyon of cost: each fake identity needs a separate sponsor risking separate funds. Mirror audits then compare sponsors, exposing clusters vouched for by one wallet.
